title: AI bosses say that AI is growing too fast

paragraphs: Tech executives are divided on AI regulation. OpenAI boss Sam Altman acknowledged public fears while urging trust in developers. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang opposed new laws and stated that companies should self-regulate product safety.

Sanders warned that AI risks could exceed those of nuclear weapons, and urged lawmakers to prevent corporations from socializing the risks while keeping the financial profits. Politicians across the political spectrum are demanding strict restrictions; however, US President Donald Trump has dismissed safety fears surrounding AI as a hoax. He argued against slowing down development because the country that leads in AI wins globally. Trump highlighted the technology’s immense economic potential and compared its value to big industries like oil and diamonds.

Experts emphasize that the United States must establish strong domestic oversight to set international standards. Tech companies often leverage the idea of a global race with China to justify moving forward without adequate laws.

paragraphs: US President Donald Trump called AI safety fears a hoax and said the country must win the global AI race. He believes AI will bring economic growth bigger than oil or diamonds.

But many people and experts disagree on how to manage this new technology. OpenAI leader Sam Altman says people should trust tech companies, while Nvidia’s CEO believes businesses should control their own safety rules without new government laws. Some politicians warned that AI could be more dangerous than nuclear weapons.

Many critics worry that big companies want all the profits, but at the same time, ordinary people will be at risk. Experts argue that the US needs strict rules to protect people and set a good example for the rest of the world.

paragraphs: US President Donald Trump says that fears about AI are not real. He wants the US to win the AI race. It will make the country strong.

Some tech leaders say that people should trust them to make AI safe. They do not want new laws. But many politicians want strong safety rules. Some politicians say that AI can be very dangerous, even more than nuclear bombs.
Some people believe that big companies only want to make money. Normal people will take all the risks. Experts say that we need good rules today to keep everyone safe in the future.
